we have made significant contributions in the area of automatic affect recognition from bodily expressions by (1) proposing a novel approach for data acquisition and annotation for affective face-andbody expressions, (2) proposing an automatic approach for affective face and body expression recognition using space-time interest point detection and Canonical Correlation Analysis, and (3), proposing a novel approach based on the temporal phase detection of affective states.

the automatic analysis of bodily expression is important for affect recognition and can be achieved using a variety of techniques, including the ones described here.
we can automatically recognize affect from the bodily expressions of the human body, and that we can also detect the temporal phases of affective expressions.
automatic affect recognition from face-and body displays can be achieved by analyzing the facial and body expressions in parallel and using a fusion approach to combine the results.
